name: Hot Purple
lede: Hot Purple is a saturated violet-magenta that crowdsourcing, not a dictionary or a dye house, put a name to.

sections.title: A crowd name, not a dictionary one
sections.body:
Our color library traces Hot Purple to the xkcd color survey of 2010, in which volunteers typed free-text names for colors shown on screen and the most popular labels for each shade were kept [1]. "Hot" here works the way it does in Hot Pink: a plain intensifier on the hue word, not a reference to temperature or to any material [1]. Who first typed this exact pairing, or whether it existed earlier, is undocumented in our sources [1].

The nearest named neighbor by measured color is [[bright-purple]], close enough that the two read as the same color at a glance; [[phlox]] sits a little further out, lighter [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: No painting in our 23,781-painting archive has a color within CIEDE2000 4 of Hot Purple covering at least 1 percent of its canvas, as photographed [3]. A violet this saturated and this bright is rare in oil paint generally, since the brightest purple pigments and dyes are a recent and largely synthetic group [3]. That describes our museum-sourced archive, not painting as a whole [3].

origin.named_after: undocumented; a crowd-sourced label from the 2010 xkcd color survey
